newsitem.title: FRANCE: TPS seen in profit end-1999/early 2000 - du Peloux.
newsitem.headline: TPS seen in profit end-1999/early 2000 - du Peloux.

text.p: French digital satellite television service Television Par Satellite should show its first profits at the end of 1999 or at the beginning of the year 2000, a TPS official said on Monday.

"The first profits are expected with a million subscribers. This could be achieved at the end of 1999, or at the beginning of the year 2000," Cyrille du Peloux, the service's managing director, told Reuters in an interview.
Du Peloux was speaking at the annual MIP television trade fair here.
TPS is operated by private terrestrial channel TF1 and majority-owned by private channel M6-Metropole TV and its parents.
TPS rival Canalsatellite, a unit of Canal Plus, expects to reach operating breakeven a year earlier, its chairman, Bruno Delacour, told Reuters on Sunday.
He said this would be triggered by a subscriber level of 850,000 to 900,000 subscribers.
Earlier on Monday Patrick Le Lay, chairman of TPS and TF1, told a news conference he still expected TPS to have 300,000 subscribers by the end of this year.
Le Lay had made the prediction earlier this month. Initially TPS was expecting to have 250,000 subscribers by the end of 1997.
